name: Internal capsule
summary: A thick V-shaped band of white matter between the caudate and thalamus medially and the lentiform nucleus laterally, through which almost every fiber connecting the cortex with the brainstem, spinal cord and thalamus must pass. The anterior limb carries frontopontine and anterior thalamic fibers, the genu the corticobulbar fibers, and the posterior limb the corticospinal tract (face to leg, anterior to posterior) with the thalamocortical sensory fibers behind them and the optic and auditory radiations in its retro- and sublenticular parts. Fed by the lenticulostriate and anterior choroidal perforators, it is the classic site of the lacunar pure motor stroke and of hypertensive hemorrhage.

anatomy.location: Between the head of the caudate and the thalamus (medial) and the lentiform nucleus (lateral), continuous above with the corona radiata and below with the crus cerebri; on axial sections the anterior limb lies between caudate head and putamen, the posterior limb between thalamus and lentiform nucleus, and the genu at the angle beside the foramen of Monro.

subdivisions.name: Anterior limb
subdivisions.note: anterior thalamic radiation, frontopontine fibers; prefrontal-caudate loops

subdivisions.name: Genu
subdivisions.note: corticobulbar fibers to the cranial nerve nuclei

subdivisions.name: Posterior limb
subdivisions.note: corticospinal tract (arm anterior, leg posterior), superior thalamic radiation (sensory), corticorubral fibers

subdivisions.name: Retrolenticular part
subdivisions.note: optic radiation and posterior thalamic radiation

function: Conduction of all corticofugal (motor) and thalamocortical (sensory and association) fibers between the cerebral cortex and the diencephalon, brainstem and spinal cord.

bestView.label: anterior limb, genu and posterior limb between the lentiform nucleus and the thalamus
posterior limb between thalamus and lentiform nucleus continuing into the crus

imaging.normalAppearance: The V-shaped white matter band around the lentiform nucleus on axial T1/T2; the posterior limb is slightly T2-dark because of dense myelin. Small acute infarcts here appear as bright DWI dots; hypertensive putaminal hemorrhage often spreads into it.

pathology.finding: Small restriction in the posterior limb.
Restriction in the posterior limb extending to the geniculate region and medial temporal lobe.

pathology.pathology: Putaminal hemorrhage extending into the capsule
pathology.finding: Hyperdense hematoma of the lentiform nucleus with capsular involvement.
T2 hyperintensity and atrophy along the posterior limb and crus after a large cortical infarct.

lesionEffects.deficit: Pure motor hemiparesis of face, arm and leg
lesionEffects.mechanism: Corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers in the genu and posterior limb
Posterior limb with the adjacent thalamocortical fibers or thalamus

examination: Power in face, arm and leg; note their similar involvement
Absence of aphasia, neglect and cortical sensory signs
pearls: Face, arm and leg equally weak with nothing cortical: the capsule
The dense hemiplegia of an internal capsule lesion comes from a tiny lesion because the fibers are packed so tightly
